traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 15 Lauraceae: trees or shrubs (very rarely the twining parasite Cassytha), every part with aromatic oil glands; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, leathery and evergreen; no stipules; flowers small, greenish or yellowish, usually in cymes or racemes, bisexual, polygamous or dioecious, regular; perianth lobes usually 6 (two whorls of 3, read as tepals); stamens in up to four whorls; ovary of one carpel, superior, rarely inferior; fruit a berry or drupe.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Lauraceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Cassythaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded evergreen. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
